notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch (curl), no blocking, robots.txt allows crawling (Shopify storefront). Discovery: main nav has a top-level 'New' link (/collections/new, og:title 'Shop Our Latest Additions!', also used as the target of homepage 'Shop New Arrivals'/'Shop new arrivals' CTA buttons -- confirms it is the sitewide New Arrivals listing). Each product-category mega-menu (Rugs, Lighting, Outdoor, Pillows & Decor, Mirrors & Art) additionally carries its own dedicated 'New ... Arrivals' promo tile -- these are NOT nested under the 'New' nav item (which has no dropdown/children of its own); they are independent, category-scoped New Arrivals listings surfaced inside each unrelated category's own menu, so they are recorded as separate sibling rows rather than as children of a 'New' parent. Furniture's mega-menu has no such tile (no dedicated Furniture New Arrivals PLP exists). Also fetched the full site collections.json (726 collections, paginated) and keyword-scanned for new/arriv/latest/just-in -- surfaced two additional zero-product handles ('lazy-susan-new', 'new-wave') which were dropped as empty listings. None of the six 'New' pages are marketing/lookbook pages -- each opened to a real, filterable product grid with its own utility-bar count. QTY METHOD: Shopify collections.json 'products_count' proven inflated site-wide (established in prior Home-Decor pass); used the rendered utility-bar 'N products' header instead throughout, and cross-verified 2 of 6 rows exactly against a full products.json pagination exhaustion (New Lighting Arrivals: header=24, products.json=24; Newest Art & Mirrors: header=14, products.json=14).
